Academic Eligibility Requirementc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/cco-gro/onto#AcademicEligibilityRequirementPattern

The name 'AcademicEligibilityRequirement' captures the universal concept of academic suitability/standing requirements without jurisdiction-specific terms. It is a subclass of cco:Condition and retains only axioms applicable to both aligned classes, satisfying the pattern's constraints on neutrality and universal applicability.
A condition that must be satisfied by a student to demonstrate they meet the academic criteria required for enrollment or continuation in an educational program, as determined by the institution.
has super-classes
Condition c
has sub-classes
Academically Suitable c, Scholastic Standing Requirement c

has super-classes
Action c, Assessment Action c

has super-classes
Evidentiary Document c, Resource c

Academic Withdrawal Resourcec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/cco-gro/onto#AcademicWithdrawalResourcePattern

The name 'AcademicWithdrawalResource' is jurisdiction-neutral, avoids program-specific terminology, and reflects the universal purpose of the classes as resources for recording withdrawal details. It satisfies the pattern's constraints by being a subclass of cco:Resource and ensuring all axioms apply universally across aligned jurisdictions.
A resource used to document or confirm a student's withdrawal from a study period, including details such as the date, time, and specific units of study affected by the withdrawal.
has super-classes
Resource c
has sub-classes
Non-Punitive Withdrawal Form c, Withdrawal Confirmation Mechanism c

Academic Yearc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/cco-gro/onto/ca#AcademicYear

For the purpose of assessment of need, the academic year is defined by the post-secondary institution and is based on the study period for which student financial assistance is required that starts between August 1 of the current year and July 31 of the following year. The academic year is subject to a maximum length of 12 months (52 weeks) and may include multiple terms or semesters, including spring and/or summer sessions.
has super-classes
Condition c
